page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance engineered with a focus on compute throughput and high-speed local temporary storage. Built on Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors, the instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs spanning 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, reaching clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem features a generous 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for modern vector and matrix instructions, including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. Memory configuration stands at 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results place the D128lds_v7 in the top tier for multi-core compute and throughput tasks. It achieves strong results in multi-threaded decompression (803.1 GB/sec in bzip3), compilation workloads (70,716.0 in Geekbench Clang), and static web serving throughput (145.81 GB/sec). Extended instruction sets benefit specialized calculation routines, demonstrated by top-tier PassMark CPU extended instructions (171,745.5) and encryption scores (142,532.58). For memory bandwidth, the instance posts a 657.87 GB/sec uncached read figure and handles up to 196.23 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary architectural trade-off of the D128lds_v7 lies in its reduced memory-to-core allocation. While standard general-purpose servers typically offer 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance provisions 2.0 GB per core, trading broad per-thread memory capacity for cost efficiency and dense multi-threaded computation. Furthermore, the 7,560 GB local NVMe array offers massive local IOPS and low latency, but workloads requiring persistent data storage will need attached network volumes, as local NVMe drives are ephemeral.

Given its performance profile, the D128lds_v7 is suited for compute-intensive batch processing, CI/CD compilation farms, high-throughput caching tiers like Redis, static content serving, and large-scale data transformation (ETL) pipelines that benefit from high multi-core density, matrix instructions, and fast temporary scratch space.
